newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Philips tops slow New York ADR market.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Philips tops slow New York ADR market.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV was among a handful of foreign companies to stand out in a slow American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) market on Monday, traders and analysts said.

Trade in most ADRs, especially those for Latin American companies, was weighed by upcoming earnings news and by the Columbus Day holiday which shut U.S. banks and the bond market. "It's a holiday in the U.S. and ... people are waiting for third-quarter earnings to come out, which has already started," said John Hellier, head of international sales and trading at Oppenheimer.
Mexican ADRs also were hit by a sudden weakening of the peso, with Telefonos de Mexico off 1/4 to 31-5/8 on volume of 714,800 shares.

The Netherlands' Philips was off one point to 36-3/4 in early afternoon after falling more than two points in Amsterdam. The decline came after the electronics giant warned operating profits were unlikely to rise in the second quarter.
"That shocked people a bit. I think people are looking for a restructuring in the near future," one trader said.
British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc rose 1-5/8 to 62-3/8 on prospects for a digital television network in Germany.
Telecom Corp of New Zealand Ltd was up 1-5/8 to 78-3/8, boosted by election results that showed lessened support for the South Pacific nation's far-left Alliance Party.
By early afternoon, 119 of the 441 ADRs trading in New York had posted gains and 120 showed declines. The remainder were unchanged.
